newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch PTT told to cut interconnection rate.
newsitem.headline: Dutch PTT told to cut interconnection rate.

text.p: Dutch post and telecoms group PTT Nederland has been ordered to cut the tariffs it charges to competitors making use of its network, the transport ministry said on Thursday.
"KPN must reduce its tariff for incoming telephone traffic (terminating access)...to 3.6 cents per minute from four (cents)," the ministry said in a statement.
It said transport minister Annemarie Jorritsma had ordered the reduction as an interim measure pending the creation of a so-called cost allocation system.

Such a system would determine the relative costs incurred by KPN -- which formerly held a monopoly in Dutch fixed-line telephony -- and its new rivals Telfort and Enertel, a consortium of Dutch regional power companies and local cable television network operators.
Telfort, a joint venture between British Telecom Plc and state-owned Dutch Railways NS, earlier asked the ministry to intervene in its long-running dispute with KPN on tariffs.
The ministry said Jorritsma had assessed KPN's tariffs for terminating and originating access respectively.
Of these, terminating access is of greatest importance to KPN's rivals as it determines the price at which their customers gain access to the KPN network when calling KPN clients.
Jorritsma found KPN had unjustifiably included a number of costs such as marketing and overheads in its terminating access tariff which warranted an initial 10 percent reduction.
However, KPN's originating access tariff was deemed fair.
The latter tariff for outgoing traffic determines the carrier selection rate -- and thus the service provider which callers choose for long-distance calls.
